basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 11.' and it opens 'Vers. 11. Percusserunt caecitate. Quoddam genus caecitatis est quod Graece aorasia'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 11. Percusserunt caecitate. Quoddam genus caecitatis est quod Graece aorasia dicitur, id est, avidentia, | qua quaedam videntur, quaedam non videntur. Sodomitae ergo alia videbant, sed ostium Lot videre non poterant. Moraliter Lot justos significat, Sodomitae invidos et detractores designant, qui quodammodo ostium quaerunt per quod ad Lot irrumpant, quando homines bona facta reprehendere volunt, sed non possunt invenire aditum reprehendendi, quia illo virtutis claustro munito corruptores mentium nihil habent quod reprehendant.
